text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 28 in history.
1520 - Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan passed through the strait which bears his name to the Pacific ocean.
1582 - Playwright and poet William Shakespeare married Anne Hathaway.
1632 - Composer Giovanni Battista Lully born in Florence; he became music master to Louis XIV and was best known for his operas "Armide" and "Alceste".
1757 - William Blake, English poet, painter and engraver, born; he wrote "Songs of Innocence" which he also illustrated. Among his best known works are illustrations to the "Book of Job".
1820 - Friedrich Engels, German socialist and associate of Karl Marx, born; he edited the second and third volumes of Marx's "Das Kapital"
1821 - Panama declared itself independent of Spain and joined the Republic of Colombia.
1859 - U.S. author Washington Irving died; he became famous for his "Sketch Book" which contained the stories of "Rip Van Winkle" and "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow".
1895 - Spanish concert pianist Jose Iturbi, who also appeared in a number of Hollywood films including "Anchors Aweigh" and "That Midnight Kiss", born.
1899 - In the second Boer War, the British under Lord Methuen defeated a force of 9,000 Boers in the battle of Modder River.
1905 - The Irish political party Sinn Fein was founded in Dublin by Arthur Griffith.
1907 - Italian author Alberto Moravia born.
1934 - U.S. bank robber George "Baby Face" Nelson was killed near Barrington, Illinois, by FBI agents.
1941 - In World War Two, the Russian army retook Rostov.
1943 - Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin met at Tehran for their first meeting together to chart the future Allied course for World War Two and decide a post-war future.
1958 - Mauritania became an autonomous republic within the French Community; two years later on this day it achieved full independence.
1962 - Wilhemina, Queen of the Netherlands from 1890-1948, died. She won much admiration for her conduct during World War Two and abdicated in 1948 in favour of her daughter.
1964 - U.S. space probe Mariner 4 was launched on a journey to Mars; it passed within 5,400 miles of Mars in July 1965.
1971 - The prime minister of Jordan, Wasfi Tell, was shot by Black September terrorists just outside the Hilton Hotel in Cairo where he was on an official visit.
1979 - An Air Zealand DC-10 on a flight from Auckland to the South Pole hit Mount Erebus in Antarctica killing all 257 people aboard.
1994 - Jeffrey Dahmer, who killed 17 young men in a 13-year orgy of dismemberment and cannibalism, was clubbed to death in prison as he cleaned a toilet.
1995 - British Prime Minister John Major and Irish counterpart John Bruton unveiled a new initiative for all-party talks on the future of the British-ruled province of Northern Ireland.
